skill.name: openmotion
skill.description: Create and edit videos with OpenMotion, recreate a reference video, or adapt an editable template. Set up the local Studio and MCP connection when missing, then continue through the matching production workflow. Use for OpenMotion installation and first use; an already-selected specialist continues directly. Repository development does not trigger video production.
skill.summary: Create, revise, and export editable video projects in local OpenMotion Studio from a brief, reference, or template.
skill.author: nexu-io

security_audit.summary: Nine backtick alerts are Markdown formatting, and the reconnaissance alert matches a restriction on what installation authorizes. The skill directs agents to retrieve a mutable installation guide and follow its setup instructions without a separate approval step. No evidence of malicious commands or credential transfer was found in the reviewed file.

remediation.issue: Runtime setup depends on a mutable external guide and can follow from a video request.
remediation.suggestion: Pin setup instructions to a reviewed release. Show the proposed commands and configuration changes, and require explicit approval before running them.

content.user_title: Create and Edit Videos in OpenMotion
content.value_statement: A video brief or reference still needs to become an editable project before you can revise it. OpenMotion routes your request to the right workflow in local Studio for editing, preview, and MP4 export.
actual_capabilities: Resume work in a connected OpenMotion Studio project.
Route a creative brief to the workflow for an original video.
Browse or adapt an existing editable video template.
Recreate a reference for one film or turn it into a reusable template.
Route scoped edits, preview, troubleshooting, and MP4 export to the production workflow.
Select a workflow for generating a single image, video, speech, or music asset.
limitations: Installing the skill alone does not install the runtime, Studio, or browser and media prerequisites.
This version uses local MCP over standard input and output, not a ChatGPT cloud endpoint.
The calling host must discover the native tools and successfully look up the project before it can confirm the connection.
Technical export validation does not confirm successful playback or visual quality.

use_cases.title: Create a product demo
use_cases.description: Turn a short brief into an editable Studio project and preview the pacing before export.

use_cases.title: Adapt a training video template
use_cases.description: Replace the lesson text in an editable template while keeping its established layout and timing.

use_cases.title: Build a reusable title sequence
use_cases.description: Use a reference you have permission to adapt as the basis for a template for future episodes.

prompt_templates.title: Find a template
prompt_templates.prompt: In my connected OpenMotion Studio, show me editable templates for a short event announcement. Do not modify a project.

prompt_templates.title: Adapt a template
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the selected template for a workshop invitation. Set the title to Design Workshop, keep the original timing, and show a preview before export.

prompt_templates.title: Create a video from a brief
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an editable 20-second product demo from my brief and supplied screenshots. Preview the opening, the feature walkthrough, and the closing title.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: plan and preview an original video

prompt_templates.title: Make a reusable reference template
prompt_templates.prompt: Use my approved reference clip to make a reusable title template. Keep titles and colors editable, preserve the existing project, and preview a sample variation.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: adapt a reference for repeated use

output_examples.input: Change only the closing title to Spring Workshop and preview it.
output_examples.output: The preview shows Spring Workshop on the closing title. The earlier scenes are unchanged, and no MP4 was exported.

output_examples.input: Turn my approved opening clip into a reusable intro template with editable titles and colors.
output_examples.output: The intro is available as an editable template in Studio. The preview shows a sample title and color change.

best_practices: Name the project and specify which scenes or settings should stay unchanged.
Use reference material and assets you have permission to adapt.
Review setup commands before approving them, and play back the finished MP4 before delivery.
anti_patterns: Mixing source and npm installations in the same setup.
Starting project edits or paid generation when the user only requested installation.
Treating the Studio browser URL as an MCP endpoint.

faq.question: Does installing the skill also install OpenMotion Studio?
faq.answer: No. The skill installs instructions only. Studio, its runtime, and browser and media prerequisites need separate setup.

faq.question: How do I know whether my host is connected?
faq.answer: The calling host must discover the native OpenMotion tools and successfully retrieve the project. A separate probe does not verify that host.

faq.question: Can I use an existing Studio installation?
faq.answer: Yes. Reuse a working installation and MCP connection. Do not mix a source installation with the npm application.

faq.question: Can I export an MP4?
faq.answer: Yes, through the production workflow in a connected workspace. Check playback and visual quality separately after export.

faq.question: Can I reuse a video reference across projects?
faq.answer: Yes. Request an editable template from a reference you have permission to adapt, rather than a recreation for a single film.

faq.question: Does this version offer a ChatGPT cloud endpoint?
faq.answer: No. This version connects through a local MCP server using standard input and output.
